headline: RapWire 24/7: Shabazz Palaces, Che’ Noir, Hit-Boy, Warner Music Group and GTA VI
body: RapWire's verified Oct. 23 afternoon carousel covers new releases from Shabazz Palaces, Che’ Noir and Hit-Boy, Warner Music Group's global sync reorganization, and fresh GTA VI map-development reporting. Every slide uses original subject-led late-1980s editorial comic art with complete readable reporting, no top banner and the official transparent RapWire mark.

Every slide uses original subject-led late-1980s editorial comic art with complete readable reporting, no top banner and the official transparent RapWire mark.
caption:
1) Shabazz Palaces’ It’s a Style Sport is now available through Sub Pop. Ishmael Butler’s 10-track return was shaped in an eight-day Seattle session with longtime collaborators, making the album a fresh statement from one of rap’s most exploratory voices.
2) Che’ Noir’s It Takes A Village is out now as a 12-track statement through Poetic Records and HiPNOTT Records. Black Thought, Ransom and Bruiser Wolf join a production roster that includes Havoc, Nottz and Conductor Williams, giving the Buffalo MC a deep cross-generational circle around her writing.
3) Hit-Boy has released The Chauncey Hollis Project II, a nine-song sequel named for the producer-rapper’s birth name and issued through Surf Club. The Alchemist, 03 Greedo, Dom Kennedy and Stacy Barthe appear across a set that leans into introspection instead of chasing a radio-sized hook.
4) Warner Music Group has unified its global sync operations across recorded music and publishing, with Ron Broitman leading the new structure. The company says the goal is a faster path for its catalog into film, television, advertising and games, a lane that can expand how rap records reach visual audiences.
5) New reporting on Rockstar’s GTA VI development says map work began around 2015, with artists building a denser world around roads narrower than those in GTA V. The game remains scheduled for Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, so every new design detail sharpens the picture of what the long build was buying.

@Rapwire247

slide_editorial_copy.headline: SHABAZZ PALACES RETURNS
slide_editorial_copy.deck: Ishmael Butler's 10-track It’s a Style Sport is out Oct. 23 via Sub Pop after an eight-day Seattle studio session. The record pushes avant-hip-hop, live-band collaboration and a more reflective chapter of his long-running project.

slide_editorial_copy.headline: CHE' NOIR BUILDS A VILLAGE
slide_editorial_copy.deck: Che' Noir's 12-track It Takes A Village arrives Oct. 23 with Black Thought, Ransom and Bruiser Wolf, backed by production from Havoc, Nottz and Conductor Williams. The Buffalo MC turns her independent lineage into a cross-generational statement.

slide_editorial_copy.headline: HIT-BOY GOES CHAUNCEY AGAIN
slide_editorial_copy.deck: Hit-Boy’s nine-song The Chauncey Hollis Project II is out Oct. 23 through Surf Club, with The Alchemist, 03 Greedo, Dom Kennedy and Stacy Barthe in the mix. He keeps the sequel focused on introspective bars over his own West Coast production.

slide_editorial_copy.headline: WARNER'S SYNC SHIFT
slide_editorial_copy.deck: Warner Music Group put Ron Broitman over a unified global sync operation spanning recorded music and publishing. The move is designed to clear one catalog faster for film, TV, advertising and games—and could change how rap records travel into visual media.

slide_editorial_copy.headline: GTA VI MAPS THE LONG GAME
slide_editorial_copy.deck: Fresh reporting says GTA VI’s map work began around 2015, with artists shaping narrower roads than GTA V and then adding denser buildings and traffic around them. The scale of the world explains why Rockstar’s long build keeps producing new design trade-offs.
